A Short Note on Margins

By Ada Paper

Margins are where a page breathes. A narrow column with generous white space on either side lets the eye rest between lines, and that rest is what makes a long read feel short.

Printers learned this centuries ago. The outer margin is wider than the inner one, so that an open book shows a single block of text framed by quiet space, not two columns pressed together at the spine.

On a screen the same rule holds. Give the text room, keep the lines to a readable length, and the page stops shouting. That is all a good margin asks for, and it is enough.
